grades.A: Direct evidence in the stated system and outcome
grades.B: Convergent evidence with a bounded transfer
grades.C: Plausible synthesis requiring a direct test

nodes.label: Constitutional variation
nodes.plain: Inherited differences in a specific, measured genetic or physiological feature

nodes.label: Perinatal conditions
nodes.plain: Conditions around birth, measured separately from later adversity

nodes.label: α₂δ / CaV2 biology
nodes.plain: Calcium-channel trafficking and distinct synapse-formation roles

nodes.label: Stress regulation
nodes.plain: HPA and autonomic responses shaped by exposure and context

nodes.label: Attention and action
nodes.plain: State-dependent attention, movement, sampling, and task persistence

nodes.label: Environment and feedback
nodes.plain: Task timing, social response, safety, resources, and available tools

nodes.label: Adaptation / masking
nodes.plain: Learned strategies that alter behavior and social exposure

nodes.label: Developmental organization
nodes.plain: Change in functional coherence, with multiple possible trajectories

nodes.label: Capacity conversion
nodes.plain: Health, practice, execution, support, opportunity, and dissemination

nodes.label: Visible output
nodes.plain: Work that is completed, taken up, and enters a public record

edges.claim: Some RCCX variants could alter endocrine or connective-tissue constraints in defined clinical subgroups.
edges.boundary: CAH-X and hEDS/HSD clinical samples; no general ADHD or giftedness inference.
edges.rival: Independent polygenic and environmental causes explain the same phenotype.

edges.claim: A single RCCX-centered constitutional route could bias broad attention style.
edges.boundary: No direct human test of this bridge; ADHD GWAS is polygenic.
edges.rival: Distributed common variation and non-genetic factors dominate.

edges.claim: Perinatal exposure could shift α₂δ/CaV2 developmental timing.
edges.boundary: Cell, rodent, and rare severe human variants do not establish this exposure-mediated bridge.
edges.rival: Subunit expression follows intrinsic developmental programs independent of the exposure.

edges.claim: A channel or synapse timing difference could contribute to later attention phenotype.
edges.boundary: No direct longitudinal common-variation evidence for this chain.
edges.rival: Later attention differences arise through other neurodevelopmental routes.

edges.claim: Early exposures can associate with later stress-regulatory biology.
edges.boundary: Human methylation studies are tissue- and site-specific, often observational; direct inheritance is unproven.
edges.rival: Shared environment, cell composition, genotype, or recall bias explains associations.

edges.claim: Physiological state can change attention and action in context.
edges.boundary: Event-rate effects are measured in ADHD tasks; hEDS autonomic findings are selected clinical observations.
edges.rival: Task learning and reward expectations explain changes without autonomic mediation.

edges.claim: Task event rate changes ADHD Go/No-Go performance patterns.
edges.boundary: Applies to studied tasks and groups; other ADHD differences remained.
edges.rival: Specific task demand rather than generalized regulatory closure.

edges.claim: Repeated mismatch may recruit learned compensatory strategies.
edges.boundary: CAT-Q measures autistic adult camouflaging; transfer to all attention phenotypes is untested.
edges.rival: Strategies reflect social learning independent of attention style.

edges.claim: Adaptation changes social feedback and future exposures.
edges.boundary: Feedback direction is theorized here; longitudinal causal estimates are absent.
edges.rival: Stable social context drives both adaptation and outcome.

edges.claim: Attention traits can change exploration choices in a controlled foraging task.
edges.boundary: Online task with an ADHD screener; no ancestral hunter type or universal advantage.
edges.rival: Risk preference or strategy differences explain patch-leaving.

edges.claim: Exposure and social context can feed back into stress regulation.
edges.boundary: Associations do not isolate a single molecular transmission route.
edges.rival: Genotype and background adversity jointly generate both.

edges.claim: Chronic regulatory load may contribute to divergent organization trajectories.
edges.boundary: Dąbrowski bifurcation is a developmental theory, not a validated binary endpoint.
edges.rival: Trajectories vary continuously with resources, treatment, and context.

edges.claim: More coherent regulation may improve the conversion of capacity into finished work.
edges.boundary: No source directly tests the full three-toggle model.
edges.rival: Resources and opportunity explain completed work without this mediator.

edges.claim: AI assistance can alter rated output in a bounded creative task.
edges.boundary: Short-story experiment; effects on scientific discovery or polymathic individuals are unknown.
edges.rival: Generic assistance improves everyone without changing phenotype selection.

edges.claim: Execution and dissemination determine which capacity becomes publicly visible.
edges.boundary: Framework-level distinction; no one multiplicative formula has been estimated.
edges.rival: Visibility is largely driven by institutional gatekeeping and luck.

edges.claim: Visible work and AI-mediated institutions may alter future selection environments.
edges.rival: Specialization and institutional control remain dominant.
